//: Root tsconfig — exists so services/orchestrator (③) can resolve the `@/*`
aliases used throughout apps/web. Per ADR-003 the orchestrator is the SAME
codebase as ① with a different entrypoint, so it legitimately imports
lib/llm, services/jd-parser and the Prisma client. tsx reads this from the
repo root, which is where the worker is started.
//noEmit: This project is TYPE-CHECKED, never compiled: ③ runs through tsx, which
does its own transpilation. Without `noEmit`, a bare `tsc -p tsconfig.json`
writes a .js beside every .ts under services/orchestrator. Those sit in the
tree, get swept up by the next `git add -A`, and shadow the real sources for
anything resolving extensionless imports. Every call site passes --noEmit
today, so this only mattered the first time someone forgot.
//include: `scripts/**/*.mjs` used to be listed below and did NOTHING. TypeScript
ignores .js and .mjs unless allowJs is on, so `tsc --listFiles` reported
zero files from scripts/ — the entry claimed coverage the build never
provided, which is worse than omitting it, because it reads as checked.
They stay out of the program on purpose: they are plain Node ESM run
directly, and enabling allowJs+checkJs reports 22 implicit-any findings
that are missing annotations rather than defects. The 23rd was real —
reap-deletions.mjs importing a .ts module under plain `node`, which throws
ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND — and that is fixed at the source (it runs under tsx
now) rather than by making the type checker responsible for noticing.
